title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from the surrounding pages. S is a base scheme and M is a rank-2 locally free O_S-module. G is GL(M) or SL(M), and PG = PGL(M). The Lie algebra of PG is the quotient End(M)/O_S, which Grothendieck writes PV (or PU). We are given sections ρ̃, σ̃ of PG. The elements ε̃_0 = σ̃^{-1}ρ̃ and ε̃_1 = ρ̃σ̃^{-1} are unipotent, and they are related by ε̃_1 = ρ̃(ε̃_0) = σ̃(ε̃_0), where ρ̃(·) and σ̃(·) mean conjugation. This is part of a normalisation of solutions of the 'loop equation', a braid-type relation in PGL_2 over an arbitrary base.

The problem (from the previous page). A unipotent section of PG need not lift uniquely to a unipotent section of G. Write ε = 1+N, with N nilpotent of square zero. Multiply by a scalar λ. Then λε is unipotent exactly when det = λ² = 1 and trace = 2λ = 2. So λ = 1+ν with 2ν = 0 and ν² = 0, which is a nontrivial possibility only over non-reduced bases where 2 is not invertible. Equivalently, the infinitesimal part of the kernel μ_2 of SL_2 → PGL_2 in characteristic 2.

The two lifts ε and ε' = λε have the same image in PG at t = 1. Their one-parameter subgroups t ↦ 1+tN and t ↦ 1+tN' are different, where N' = (1+ν)N + ν.

This page proves the claim. The derivatives at t = 0 of the induced maps G_a → PG are the classes Ñ and Ñ' in End(M)/O_S, and Ñ' = (1+ν)Ñ. Since Ñ is a nowhere-vanishing section of a locally free module (locally part of a basis), νÑ = 0 forces ν = 0, hence λ = 1.

Conclusion. The correct data is not just ρ̃, σ̃ in PG, but also parametrised one-parameter additive subgroups ε̃_0, ε̃_1 : G_a → PG (formula 49), compatible by (50): ε̃_1 = ρ̃(ε̃_0) = σ̃(ε̃_0) as homomorphisms. Equivalently, one chooses a unipotent lift ε_0 of ε̃_0, which is not a priori unique, and deduces ε_1 = ρ̃(ε_0) = σ̃(ε_0). The margin adds that this choice is what is needed to force a relation σ^{-1}ρ = λ·ε_0, and hence σ(ε_0) = ρ(ε_0).

The next page turns this into a Proposition. A strict one-parameter subgroup G_a → PG lifts uniquely to t ↦ 1+tN_i in G. Then, for lifts ρ, σ, one has ε_0 = -λ_0σ^{-1}ρ for a unique scalar λ_0, which can be normalised to 1. Uniqueness of the lift holds because G_a is reduced and connected, so it admits no nontrivial pointed maps to μ_2.
errors: In (50), conjugation is written as ρ(ε̃_0) and σ(ε̃_0) without tildes, although only ρ̃ and σ̃ are given at this stage. This is harmless, since conjugation by a lift depends only on its image in PG.

The non-vanishing of Ñ, which is used to conclude ν = 0, needs the hypothesis that ε is a 'regular' (everywhere non-trivial) unipotent, i.e. N nowhere zero modulo scalars. It is only implicit here (the inserted 'rég.' in the margin) and is made explicit as 'strict' on the next page.

ideas.what: Unipotent elements of PGL_2 lift to unipotent elements of SL_2/GL_2 only up to scalars λ with λ²=1 and 2λ=2, i.e. λ = 1+ν with 2ν = ν² = 0. These are nontrivial over non-reduced bases of characteristic 2.
ideas.modern_name: Non-étaleness of the central isogeny SL_2 → PGL_2 in characteristic 2 (infinitesimal kernel μ_2)
ideas.where_published: General framework in SGA 3; this specific remark is not, as far as known.

ideas.what: Replacing unipotent elements by parametrised one-parameter additive subgroups G_a → PG, which lift uniquely through the isogeny; the differential at 0 detects the difference between lifts.
ideas.modern_name: Lifting homomorphisms from G_a through a central isogeny / rigidity of maps from a reduced connected scheme to a finite infinitesimal kernel

ideas.what: Normalisation of the data (ρ̃, σ̃, ε̃_0) for the loop equation in PGL_2 over an arbitrary base, so that it can be lifted to (ρ, σ, ε_0, ε_1) in GL_2 with σ^{-1}ρ = -λ_0 ε_0.
ideas.modern_name: Integral/scheme-theoretic moduli of braid-relation representations into PGL_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: unclear; unpublished Grothendieck work on the 'équation des lacets'

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine technical step. In characteristic 2, over non-reduced bases, unipotent lifts from PGL_2 are non-unique, so Grothendieck adds parametrised G_a-subgroups to the data. It shows his insistence on working over arbitrary bases, but contains nothing new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'section de PU' is more likely 'PV' (consistent with the previous page, 'M/O_S ≃ PV').
The interlinear insertion reads roughly 'des relèvements unip. et rég.' (unipotent and regular lifts).
In (50) the image shows ρ(ε̃_0), σ(ε̃_0) without tildes on ρ and σ.
Left margin: 'pour assurer nécessairement une relation σ^{-1}ρ = λ∘ε_0, donc σ(ε_0) = ρ(ε_0)'; the struck '=' is replaced.
